title: E-Commerce Checkout Automation Suite
summary: End-to-end Playwright automation framework covering the full checkout journey across 3 payment gateways.
overview: The client's checkout flow spanned guest checkout, saved cards, wallets and 3 payment gateways. Manual regression before every release took 2 full QA days and still missed edge cases in coupon stacking and currency conversion.
approach: Built a Page Object Model framework in Playwright + TypeScript with fixtures for auth, cart seeding and mock payment responses.
Designed a data-driven test matrix covering 45 checkout scenarios across currencies, coupons and payment methods.
Wired the suite into GitHub Actions with parallel sharding (6 workers) and Allure HTML reporting on every PR.
Added visual regression checks on the payment summary screen using Playwright's screenshot assertions.
findings: Found a race condition where double-clicking 'Place Order' created duplicate charges under slow network throttling.
Caught a currency rounding bug that under-charged EUR customers by up to 0.02 per order.
Identified that coupon stacking silently failed when two percentage-based coupons were applied together.

title: REST API Contract & Load Testing Framework
summary: API test suite with schema validation, contract testing and load benchmarks for a fintech microservices backend.
overview: A fintech client's 14 microservices had no contract tests, causing breaking changes to slip into staging repeatedly. Needed a suite that could run in under 5 minutes as part of the deploy pipeline.
approach: Authored 200+ Postman/Newman collections with JSON schema validation for every response.
Introduced contract tests using Pact between the payments and ledger services.
Built a lightweight load test harness with k6 to benchmark p95 latency under 500 concurrent users.
Integrated Newman + k6 runs into GitLab CI with Slack alerts on failure.
findings: Discovered the ledger service silently dropped the 'idempotency-key' header, risking duplicate transactions.
Found p95 latency spiked to 3.2s under load on the balance endpoint due to a missing DB index.
Caught 3 breaking schema changes before they reached staging in the first month alone.

title: CI/CD Quality Gates for Multi-Team Monorepo
summary: Designed automated quality gates (lint, unit, E2E, coverage thresholds) for a 30-engineer monorepo.
overview: With 30 engineers pushing to a single monorepo, release quality was inconsistent — some PRs merged with failing tests silently ignored. The team needed enforced quality gates without slowing everyone down.
approach: Set up Jenkins multibranch pipelines with staged gates: lint → unit → integration → E2E smoke.
Configured branch protection so merges require green E2E smoke suite (Playwright) on a preview environment.
Introduced coverage thresholds (80% lines) enforced via Jest with a merge-blocking check.
Built a dashboard (Grafana) tracking flaky test rate and pipeline duration over time.
findings: Identified 14 flaky tests responsible for 60% of false-positive pipeline failures; stabilized with proper waits.
Reduced average PR pipeline time from 22 minutes to 9 minutes via parallelization and caching.
Prevented 5 production incidents in the first quarter by blocking merges on failing smoke tests.

title: Automated Excel Test Reporting Dashboard
summary: A VBA + Python powered reporting pipeline that turns raw test run logs into stakeholder-ready Excel dashboards.
overview: Stakeholders wanted a readable weekly QA status report, but the team was manually copy-pasting test results into Excel every Friday — taking 3+ hours and prone to errors.
approach: Wrote a Python script to parse JUnit/Allure XML output and normalize results into a structured dataset.
Built an Excel template with pivot tables, conditional formatting and a pass/fail trend chart, auto-refreshed via openpyxl.
Automated the whole pipeline with a scheduled task that emails the report every Friday at 5 PM.
Added a 'QA status convention' color legend (Green/Amber/Red) tied to defect severity and pass rate thresholds.
findings: Eliminated 3+ hours of manual reporting work per week for the QA team.
Surfaced a recurring module (claims-upload) with a consistently declining pass rate, prompting a focused test sprint.
Standardized how 'release readiness' was communicated to non-technical stakeholders.

title: JMeter Performance & Load Testing Suite
summary: Load, stress and performance testing framework validating API response times and system stability under concurrent user load.
overview: Ahead of a major release, the client had no visibility into how the platform behaved under real-world concurrent load, risking downtime during peak traffic. The team needed repeatable load tests integrated into the release process, not one-off manual checks.
approach: Modeled realistic user journeys with JMeter Thread Groups, driven by CSV test data for login, search and checkout flows.
Ramped load gradually (50 to 1000 concurrent users) to identify the breaking point rather than testing only at a single fixed load.
Correlated JMeter results (p90/p95/p99 response time, throughput, error rate) with server-side metrics (CPU, memory, DB query time) to pinpoint bottlenecks.
Automated test execution via a scheduled Jenkins job, converting raw .jtl results into a stakeholder-readable HTML report after every run.
findings: Identified a missing database index causing p95 latency to spike to 4.1s at 400+ concurrent users.
Found the session store became a bottleneck above 600 concurrent users, informing a caching layer decision.
Established a baseline performance budget the team now checks before every major release.

title: Mobile App Test Automation (iOS & Android)
summary: Cross-platform mobile test automation framework covering critical user flows on real devices and emulators for a field-operations app.
overview: A field-operations app used by inspectors on Android and iOS had no automated coverage, so every release relied on slow, inconsistent manual regression across both platforms and multiple device models.
approach: Built a cross-platform Appium framework with a shared Page Object layer for Android and iOS to avoid duplicating test logic.
Covered critical workflows: login, offline data capture, photo upload, GPS-tagged inspections, and sync-on-reconnect.
Ran the suite across real devices and emulators via BrowserStack App Automate for broader device/OS coverage.
Integrated test runs into CI so every build was validated on both platforms before QA sign-off.
findings: Caught a data-loss bug where offline-captured inspections were silently dropped if the app was backgrounded during sync.
Found GPS coordinates were occasionally truncated on specific Android OEM devices, affecting inspection accuracy.
Reduced manual regression time per release from 2 days to under 3 hours.

title: SQL Data Integrity & Loan Reconciliation Testing
summary: Database validation suite verifying EMI calculations, repayment schedules and transaction history against expected business rules for a loan platform.
overview: In a loan origination and management system, a wrong EMI, repayment schedule or foreclosure amount is a financial and compliance problem, not just a UI bug. UI-level checks could not prove that the values stored in the backend were correct.
approach: Wrote SQL validation queries that recompute EMI, interest and outstanding principal independently and compare them with the values stored by the application.
Verified repayment schedules, customer details and transaction history across the loan lifecycle, from lead creation to loan closure.
Checked data consistency between modules after each workflow stage, including approval, sanction, repayment and foreclosure.
Packaged the queries as a reusable regression set that was re-run for every release and after data-affecting fixes.
findings: Compared stored values with independently calculated ones to catch calculation mismatches that were invisible on the UI.
Surfaced inconsistent records between modules when a workflow stage was skipped or reversed.
Gave developers exact record-level evidence in defect reports, which shortened the fix cycle.

title: OWASP-Aware Security Testing in the QA Cycle
summary: Security-focused checks layered into functional testing: authentication, session handling, access control and input validation.
overview: Security issues were usually found late, after release. The goal was to catch the common, high-impact classes of vulnerability during normal QA, without waiting for a separate penetration test.
approach: Mapped test cases to the OWASP Top 10 risks that are realistic for a QA-level pass: broken access control, injection, and authentication failures.
Tested role-based access control by trying privileged actions and URLs with lower-privileged accounts.
Exercised session handling: expiry, logout, concurrent sessions and re-use of old tokens.
Fuzzed inputs with special characters, oversized values and script payloads, and checked API responses for leaked details.
findings: Checked that restricted pages and API endpoints reject users who lack the required role.
Verified that sessions end correctly on logout and expiry.
Confirmed that error messages and API responses do not expose stack traces or internal details.

title: Selenium + TestNG Cross-Browser Regression Suite
summary: Java-based Selenium WebDriver framework with TestNG, run in Jenkins across Chrome, Firefox and Edge.
overview: The loan platform had long, repetitive regression flows that were slow to verify by hand before every release and had to behave the same in Chrome, Firefox and Edge.
approach: Built a Selenium WebDriver framework in Java using the Page Object Model with TestNG for grouping, priorities and data providers.
Automated the high-value regression flows end to end, from lead creation to loan closure.
Ran the suite on Chrome, Firefox and Edge to catch browser-specific rendering and behaviour differences.
Integrated the suite with Maven and Jenkins for scheduled and on-demand executions with HTML reports.
findings: Cross-browser runs exposed layout and interaction differences that single-browser manual testing missed.
Scheduled Jenkins runs gave the team a regression result before each release candidate.
Stable page objects kept maintenance low when the UI changed.

title: GIS & Geo-Location Functional Testing
summary: Functional, integration and UAT testing of map-based project monitoring and field inspection workflows on web and mobile.
overview: A national infrastructure platform tracks projects, contracts and inspections on maps, with field teams using a mobile app. Map data, locations and role-based access all had to be right before each release.
approach: Designed test scenarios and test cases from the BRD and FRS, covering project, contract and inspection modules.
Verified map visualisation, location-based project tracking and inspection modules on web and mobile.
Validated field inspection workflows on Android and iOS devices, including location capture.
Ran functional, regression, smoke, sanity, integration and end-to-end cycles, finishing with UAT and post-release smoke testing.
findings: Location and map behaviour was checked against inspection records, not only visually.
Role-based access was verified for each stakeholder type across modules.
Defects were logged in Jira with reproduction steps and device details to speed up fixes.

title: Test Design, RTM & UAT Management
summary: Structured manual testing: test plans, traceability matrix, defect lifecycle in Jira and UAT sign-off support.
overview: Enterprise releases need proof that every requirement is covered and that business users have signed off. This work covers the planning and documentation side of QA that makes releases auditable.
approach: Prepared test plans, test scenarios and test cases from business requirements, with test data for each scenario.
Maintained a Requirement Traceability Matrix to show that every requirement had test coverage.
Ran the defect lifecycle in Jira: log, triage, retest and close, with clear reproduction steps.
Supported UAT with business users and release validation, including production deployment and post-release smoke testing.
findings: Traceability exposed requirements without any test coverage before execution began.
Consistent defect reports reduced back-and-forth between QA and developers.
UAT sign-off was easier to obtain because coverage and results were documented.
